title: Axios
definition: Axios is a popular third-party HTTP client library for the browser and Node.js. It acts as a wrapper around `XMLHttpRequest` (or standard HTTP in Node) to simplify requests.
simpleExplanation: If `fetch` is a standard manual transmission car, `axios` is an automatic luxury car. It does exactly the same job (gets you from point A to point B), but Axios automatically shifts gears for you—like automatically parsing JSON, automatically throwing errors on 404s, and letting you set default headers easily.
realWorldExample: An enterprise app sets up an `axios.create()` instance with a `baseURL` of `api.company.com` and an interceptor that automatically attaches a JWT Auth token to every single request made by the app.
useCases: Complex enterprise applications requiring request interceptors
Apps making hundreds of API calls where reducing boilerplate (like `.json()`) is helpful

answers.question: Why use Axios instead of Fetch?
answers.answer: 1. It automatically parses JSON responses. 2. It automatically rejects Promises on HTTP error statuses (4xx/5xx). 3. It supports request/response interceptors. 4. It supports upload progress out-of-the-box. 5. It automatically sets XSRF protection headers.

answers.question: What is an Interceptor?
answers.answer: Interceptors allow you to run code or modify requests/responses BEFORE they are sent or given to your `then/catch` block. For example, automatically adding an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header to every outgoing request.

answers.question: Is Axios faster than Fetch?
answers.answer: No. Both send standard HTTP requests over the network. The performance difference is practically zero. The benefit is entirely Developer Experience (DX).
